  "explanation": "The text restricts to the 2^{n+1}-2 nonempty proper subsets, whose sums lie in the open interval (0,1); the 2^{n+1}-3 gaps sum to less than 1, so pigeonhole gives only a gap < 1/(2^{n+1}-3) > d. The inference to (11) is a non-sequitur, and the objection's counterexample (n=1, a=(0.9,0.1): only sums 0.1 and 0.9, gap 0.8 > 1/3) shows (11)/(12) is actually false as stated. No other passage derives the near-equal subset pair, so L3.2 is not established. The standard fix — use all 2^{n+1} sums in [0,1], giving 2^{n+1}-1 gaps summing to 1 — is a one-sentence edit; the rest of Section 5 (including the empty A or B case) then goes through.",
